In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

When big tech companies owned your phones, they could make money on all sorts of services.

options.text: When your phones are owned by big tech companies, they could make money on all sorts of services.
When your phones were owned by big tech companies, they could make money on all sorts of services.
When your phone were being owned by big tech companies, they could make money on all sorts of services.
When your phones owned big tech companies, they could make money on all sorts of services.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 i.e.** ****When your phones were owned by big tech companies, they could make money on all sorts of services.**

__Explanation__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e97c856a86e7f9a2254b6d21594beffe8b2a2afbb0c5bd00cd60b251c8f9881c.png] 

While converting a sentence to passive voice:

 
• Find the subject and object of the sentence and exchange their places.
 
• Here the question is given in **Active** Voice so it has to be changed into Passive Voice.
 
 
• ​'Your phones' becomes the subject and **'big tech companies' **becomes the object
 
 
 
• The preposition **'by**' is used the object.
 
• '**V₂**' in active voice changes to **'was/were + V₃' **in passive voice.
 
• Lining up the remaining part of the sentence: they could make money on all sorts of services.

Thus, the sentence becomes: ***When your phones were owned by big tech companies, they could make money on all sorts of services.***

​Bob Tilman says that he was not happy about the announcement.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **3**

The given statement is in **>Direct Speech and in the simple present tense.

On conversion into; Indirect Speech, the given sentence will become: Bob Tilman confessed that he was not happy about the announcement.

Modals that DO NOT Change: Would, Could, Might, Should, Ought to.

When converting the statement into Indirect Speech:

1) the words of the speaker are not written in quotes. 

2) usually, the word ‘that’ is used to convey the words of the speaker.

3) the original tense of the statement is changed accordingly.

Given below are the rules of tense conversion in Direct to Indirect Speech and vice verse:

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

John said, "When I am bored, I cook."

options.text: John said that when he was bored, he cooked
John said that when he is bored, he will cook.
John said that when cooked he was bored.
John said that when he is bored, he cooks.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. *John said that when he was bored, he cooked.*

__
 
• We make changes in tenses of reported speech only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• When the reported speech is an assertive sentence, we follow these steps-
 
 
• Reporting verb 'said to' is changed into told.
 
• connector 'that' is used in place of commas.
 
• Tense of reported speech is changed accordingly. (in above sentence- 'Simple present' changes into 'Simple Past')
 
• personal Pronouns of reported speech are changed as per subject and object of reporting verb. Here, the second person- 'I' will change into 'he' as per **Subject** - 'John'.
 
 

By following these steps, we get the **final sentence**__ - *" John said that when he was bored, he cooked."*
